verdict.line: You lose the early trades and the all-in race, but Nasus still wins this matchup 54.7% of the time over 265 games because the lane flips once your Q is stacked and Frozen Heart is online.

brief.thesis: Garen's kit is built to punish you before you have a stack count or an item spike: Decisive Strike (Q, 8s cooldown) breaks any slow you land and silences on hit, and Judgment (E, 13/12/11/10/9s cooldown) is a free AoE spin that chips you while his Perseverance passive heals it back if you don't keep pressure on. Nasus has no answer to that burst at levels 1-5, which is why OP.GG gives Garen both the lane and solo-kill edge — but none of his tools scale, while Siphoning Strike stacks and Fury of the Sands do, which is why the head-to-head win rate still favors you.

theirWindow.when: Q is up and he's walking at you
theirWindow.what: He's about to break any Wither slow and silence your response. Don't commit your own trade into this — back off a step or eat the auto and reset rather than fighting into the silence.

yourWindow.what: Land Wither (W, 15-11s cooldown, 700 range) before he commits to Judgment, then follow with Fury of the Sands (R, 120s cooldown) once it's online — his Perseverance passive only heals when he hasn't been hit recently, so sustained pressure after R removes his sustain entirely.

powerCurve.note: Decisive Strike silence wins short trades outright
Judgment cooldown drops, still out-trades you
Fury of the Sands lets you threaten back
Stacked Q and Trinity Force spike trades
Frozen Heart, Spirit Visage close the gap fully

start.why: 52.1% win rate over 234 games — the flat damage reduction and passive regen let you eat his Judgment poke and keep farming under pressure instead of losing HP every wave.

boots.why: 53.8% win rate over 117 games; Garen's damage is entirely auto-attack and physical-spin based, so the flat reduction to basic attacks directly undercuts his trade pattern.

core.why: The damage and attack speed spike is what turns your stacked Q into real trade threat instead of just a farming tool.
Armor plus the attack speed reduction in melee range directly cuts into Judgment's effective damage and his auto-trade frequency — this is the item that flips the lane.
Boosts Soul Eater lifesteal so you win extended skirmishes once you've closed the stat gap, matching the 56.8% win rate over 44 games on this exact path.

situational.when: you want the armor and a slow proc online earlier instead of waiting on full Trinity Force (70% win rate over 10 games on this path)
the game runs long and you need more teamfight control and tankiness than straight damage
garen is building lifesteal or healing through your Spirit Fire armor shred

runes.keystoneWhy: The run speed and heal-on-hit proc helps you reposition out of Judgment's range and sustains your Soul Eater-boosted farming pattern while you're behind in trades — this is the page run in 48.1% of games at 47% win rate.

summoners.why: 54.4% win rate, the highest of the three combinations run in this matchup. Teleport lets you reset and relieve wave pressure without conceding CS while you're behind on trades, and Flash is your out from a committed Decisive Strike engage.

playing.title: Prioritize Q stacks over trades
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike's cooldown (8/7/6/5/4s) rewards last-hitting over poking — every kill you take with it compounds your future damage, so farm through early disadvantage rather than forcing fights you lose.

playing.title: Never trade into an available Q
playing.detail: Decisive Strike breaks your Wither slow and silences on hit, shutting down your only disengage tool. Wait for it to be on cooldown before you commit to anything.

playing.title: Wither before he spins
playing.detail: Landing W at 700 range before he engages with Judgment cuts into the attack speed and movement that make his spin and follow-up autos hurt.

playing.title: All-in only after level 6
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands is your first real kill threat — OP.GG's own read is to look for the kill when your ultimate is up, since his Perseverance passive stops healing once he's taken recent damage.

playing.title: Don't stand in extended spin trades
playing.detail: Judgment's cooldown falls to 9s at max rank and it's a free area hit around him — land your Q, then leave, rather than standing in repeated exchanges.

playing.title: Mark Frozen Heart as your power spike
playing.detail: Once it completes behind Trinity Force, his auto-attack and spin damage both drop noticeably — this is the point the lane shape goes from 'them' to 'you.'

playing.title: Save all-ins for post-Spirit Visage
playing.detail: The lifesteal boost to Soul Eater is what lets you win drawn-out skirmishes outright — don't force a long fight before this item is up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win rates come from measured games on the current patch via OP.GG; the cooldown timings, trade-window reasoning, and power curve are my own read of the ability kits.

stats.opponentTip: Keep your distance when Garen has his Conqueror stacks up. Focus on farming with [Q] foremost, and try go in for the kill when Unsealed Spellbook + Fury of the Sands [R] come off cooldown.
